question: Who among the following was widely remembered for hoisting the Indian National flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan, Bombay during a Quit India Movement in 1942?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aruna Asaf Ali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aruna Asaf Ali** was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement.
 
• She is widely remembered for hoisting the Indian National flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay during the Quit India Movement in 1942.
 
• Her act of defiance made her an iconic figure in the struggle against British colonial rule.
 
• Due to her fearless participation, she was affectionately called the "Grand Old Lady of Indian Independence."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quit India Movement**

 
 
• The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee (AICC).
 
• The movement called for an end to British rule in India and was marked by mass protests and acts of civil disobedience.
 
• The British government responded with mass detentions, and most of the Indian National Congress leadership, including Gandhi, was imprisoned.
 
• The movement is considered a crucial step towards India's independence, which was eventually achieved in 1947.
 
 
 
• **Gowalia Tank Maidan**
 
 
• Also known as August Kranti Maidan, this ground in Mumbai is historically significant for being the site where the Quit India Movement was launched.
 
• On 8 August 1942, the AICC passed the Quit India resolution here, making it a landmark in India's freedom struggle.
 
• The ground now has a memorial to commemorate the movement and the leaders who participated in it.
 
 
 
• **Aruna Asaf Ali's Contributions**
 
 
• Aside from her role in the Quit India Movement, Aruna Asaf Ali was also a social activist and a publisher.
 
• She edited the Congress party's mouthpiece, "Inquilab," which was used to spread the message of independence and mobilize support.
 
• After independence, she continued to work for social causes and was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1997.
